# Sightline release notes

## 1.99.0 · Oct 24, 2026

Your assistant can add holidays, and check its work before sending.

### New

- **Assistant changes can add and remove holidays** (Assistant). An assistant can add a day off for everyone, add a range such as a winter shutdown (stored as its working days, like the Holidays table does), or remove a holiday. The review shows what each one moves. *Where:* Assistant changes; Settings, Calendar, Holidays

### Improved

- **The assistant helper checks a batch before it sends it** (Assistant). sightline-app.py check reads the batch against the context your assistant read, with no page open, and names each problem: an unknown action, a missing or extra argument, a bad date, a new item with no id, or a batch written against an older plan. send and run make the same check and send nothing if it fails. *Where:* tools/sightline-app.py

## 1.98.0 · Oct 24, 2026

Assistant changes can apply on their own.

### New

- **Choose whether your assistant's changes wait for you** (Assistant). Pick a level for each plan: wait for your review, apply routine changes on their own, or apply everything. Deletes wait for you unless you choose everything, and deleting an initiative with Jira-linked work always waits. Each batch that applies is one quick update you can Undo. *Where:* Assistant panel, When your assistant writes changes
- **A change that can't apply says why instead of waiting quietly** (Assistant). A batch written against an older version of the plan, one more than an hour old, or one that arrives while you have unsaved edits isn't applied on its own, and your assistant is told why. While the page is open, even in a background tab, it tells your assistant every 30 seconds that it's there, so the assistant knows when nobody's listening. *Where:* Assistant panel; the results and status files in your private folder

### Improved

- **Meeting notes skill records decisions, risks and links** (Assistant). The meeting-to-plan skill now records agreed decisions, risks, starts-after links and milestones as changes, instead of listing them for you to enter by hand. *Where:* Assistant panel, Planning skills

## 1.97.1 · Oct 24, 2026

The timeline stays where you scrolled.

### Fixed

- **The timeline no longer jumps back to the top** (Timeline). When the chart redraws, for example after a Jira sync, an assistant update, a teammate's save, or when you click Start editing or Done editing, the timeline stays on the rows you were looking at. *Where:* Timeline, in both Weeks and Days

## 1.97.0 · Oct 24, 2026

Your assistant can do the whole replan.

### New

- **Assistant changes cover links, people, milestones, gates, risks and decisions** (Assistant). An assistant's changes can now add and remove starts-after links, delete initiatives, add and rename workstreams, set people's roles, allocation and workstream, add milestones with what they're done after, add gates, and add or update risks and decisions. You review them together and apply them with one click. *Where:* Roadmap, Assistant changes

### Improved

- **Assistant changes say what they move and refuse what the chart would refuse** (Assistant). Before you apply, each change lists every item it moves, with both dates and how much later. A link that would make a loop, a link inside one initiative, dates Jira sets, and work landing in blacked-out time are refused with the reason, the same as when you edit by hand. *Where:* Roadmap, Assistant changes

## 1.96.1 · Oct 24, 2026

Dragging on the chart follows the same rules as editing.

### Fixed

- **Dragged items are stamped and kept out of blacked-out time** (Timeline). When you drag an initiative, task or milestone on the chart, the change records who made it and when, like any other edit, and a drag that would land outside its workstream's dates is refused with the reason. *Where:* Timeline, dragging initiatives, tasks and milestones

## 1.96.0 · Oct 24, 2026

Give your external assistant the planning picture.

### Improved

- **Plan with capacity, dependencies, risks and decisions** (Assistant context). Your assistant context includes people, allocation and availability, workstream membership, dependencies, gates, milestones, risks and decisions. It calculates capacity and known Jira demand across the loaded active and future sprints. Parked work stays visible, and exact coverage counts explain any data omitted to fit the export. Notes and time-off descriptions stay excluded. *Where:* The private assistant folder and manual assistant context export

Take your plan from first idea to team conversation.

## 1.93.1 · Oct 23, 2026

Keep context when following up with your assistant.

### Fixed

- **Retain the selected outcome or quarters in conversation history** (Assistant). Follow-up requests retain the stable outcome IDs or quarters that belonged to earlier questions, including when you switch outcomes. Historical selections are labeled as earlier context. Requests keep complete recent turns within the existing message limit and preserve the full question length.

## 1.93.0 · Oct 23, 2026

Describe a plan change in one message.

### Improved

- **Start with your notes and see what the assistant is working on** (Assistant). Plan with AI opens an empty composer with the selected quarters in Working on. Ask assistant about this selects an outcome by its stable ID. Paste notes or describe a change and Send once; the selection travels with the request. The composer comes first, with setup and file details below. *Where:* Product updates → Roadmap → Plan with AI, or open an outcome → Ask assistant about this.

### Fixed

- **Keep roadmap ideas when opening your assistant** (Drafts). Unsubmitted roadmap ideas stay with their plan during navigation and redraws in this tab's session. A successful submission clears only the text that was submitted. Untouched assistant starters follow a new selection; a question you have written keeps its original context until you choose Switch context.

## 1.92.0 · Oct 23, 2026

Plan four quarters with your assistant.

### New

- **Focus on four quarters and ask about an outcome** (Roadmap). Choose a starting calendar quarter for a four-quarter roadmap, or switch to Long range. Work outside the window stays counted and recoverable. Plan with AI prepares a question using the displayed quarters; each outcome has Ask assistant about this. Questions keep existing drafts and wait for Send. *Where:* Product updates → Roadmap. Horizon choices stay in this browser; plan contents are unchanged.

- **Check for a reply before your first planning conversation** (Assistant). Test reply sends a short question with the saved plan context through your configured companion and preserves your unfinished message. A matching response confirms a reply for that snapshot; test responses cannot introduce proposed changes. Starter questions help organize roadmap notes or review gaps. *Where:* Connect assistant → Test reply, with the local companion configured and running.

### Fixed

- **See the welcome screen and know what Today can assess** (Getting started). A fresh browser renders the welcome screen immediately. Today offers a planning step when no work is loaded, explains when Jira data is needed, and qualifies quiet summaries when connected data is stale or incomplete.

## 1.91.0 · Oct 10, 2026

Talk through changes to your plan.

- **Turn a planning conversation into reviewed changes** (Assistant). Ask questions, capture ideas, and refine proposed changes in the assistant panel. An optional local companion connects to your company's Chat Completions endpoint using a separate private configuration file. Replies use the saved plan and Planning guide; proposed changes wait for review and Apply, with normal undo and shared Save controls. *Where:* Connect assistant → conversation, with the local companion running against the same private assistant folder.

Project guidance for your assistant.

## 1.89.0 · Oct 10, 2026

A clearer way to open Sightline.

### Improved

- **Find the ready-to-use app** (Getting started). The repository start page links to the built app and explains how to open your separate plan file. If you open the development template, a notice points to the app in a new tab while keeping your current work available.

## 1.88.1 · Oct 9, 2026

Safer reconnects and more reliable Find.

### Fixed

- **Keep edits with their original plan** (Recovery). When you have browser edits, reconnecting stops if the file now contains a different plan. Your edits stay intact so you can download them before opening another plan.
- **Reveal milestones hidden by a people filter** (Find). Finding a milestone clears a people filter when it would keep the milestone hidden. Restore previous view brings back your original filter.

## 1.88.0 · Oct 9, 2026

Safer updates and easier daily work.

### Improved

- **Reach routine work directly** (Navigation). Sort Jira work is available under Work. Choose yourself in the toolbar to use Mine and author your updates. Find reveals matching milestones, gates and notes even when filters or layers hide them, with an option to restore your previous view.
- **See feedback and keep your place** (Usability). Status messages remain visible on narrower screens. Filters retain keyboard focus after updating, and Today names the person who decides each due decision, including when no decider is set.
- **Refresh the screen you are using** (Performance). Other workspaces leave the hidden Timeline and setup tables alone. Text edits update the plan immediately and combine derived screen updates while you type; returning to a workspace renders current data.

### Fixed

- **Keep unsaved work during lock and reconnect problems** (Recovery). A teammate's active edit lock leaves your plan, undo history and recovery draft intact. Reconnecting compares the saved file with your original version and preserves your current edits before merging or asking you to resolve a conflict.
- **Keep the message you are writing** (Notes). Refreshing Jira or redrawing details keeps unsent notes, quick updates and blocker explanations for each item in this session, including your cursor position. Submitting clears only the message that was sent.
- **Refuse oversized updates without changing the plan** (Amendments). Deliverable limits are checked on a private candidate before an update reaches the live plan. Repeated initiative and task additions with the same details stay completed, including changes that add an item and then set its fields.
- **Count unfinished board work consistently** (Jira metrics). Sprint history follows the board's final column when determining completed work, matching the page. An issue in a non-final review column stays unfinished even if Jira categorizes its status as done. Earlier recorded days are retained.

## 1.87.0 · Oct 8, 2026

Clearer shared-file refresh and recovery.

### New

- **Review another copy before recovering work** (Recovery). Compare a recovery copy with the current shared file and download backups. Choose deliberately whether to bring that copy into the editor, then review it before saving. *Where:* File, Review another copy.

### Improved

- **Check for teammates' updates automatically** (Shared files). Shared plans check the local file every 15 seconds by default. An explicit choice to turn checks off is remembered. Automatic checks wait while you type, drag or use a dialog.
- **Know what saved means** (Shared files). Shared-file status distinguishes a local save from OneDrive synchronization and shows when the local file was last checked. Check OneDrive itself to confirm cloud synchronization.

## 1.86.0 · Oct 8, 2026

Clearer workspaces and a connected assistant.

### New

- **Work, Delivery and Product updates** (Navigation). Find Today and Sprint under Work; Timeline, Capacity, Status update, Decisions and Risks under Delivery; Roadmap and release notes under Product updates. Settings holds the team, calendar and Jira connection. Each group remembers where you were. *Where:* The main navigation.
- **Connect your assistant once** (Assistant). Choose a private folder. Sightline keeps context and results current; your assistant writes proposed changes for you to review. Shared context comes from the confirmed saved file. Reconnect when browser permission expires. *Where:* Connect assistant in the toolbar; Edge or Chrome.

### Improved

- **Controls match the view you are using** (Scope). View and filter controls appear on Timeline and Capacity, where they apply. Roadmap and Status update clearly describe the whole plan. Your Timeline filters stay ready for when you return.
- **Common actions first** (Details). Initiative and task details keep routine updates visible and put organizing or moving the item behind a disclosure. Deliverable timing explains its source and separates target windows from commitments.
- **Refresh only what changed for the assistant** (Performance). Changing views leaves unchanged assistant context alone. Export lookups are indexed, and navigation uses cached controls so it stays cheap as more screens are opened.

### Fixed

- **Saved views remember which sources you chose** (Views). Personal and team views now save and restore All sources, Jira only or Jira + mine. Changing sources marks the view modified, and All work restores all sources. *Where:* Timeline and Capacity saved views.

## 1.85.0 · Sep 30, 2026

Rows by epic follow every parent link.

### New

- **Rows by epic go past the epic** (Timeline). Rows by epic now nest by any parent link, not only epics: an epic under its feature, the feature under its initiative, as deep as Jira goes. Each row says what it is (Feature, Initiative), and a task linked to a sub-task sits on its story's epic. *Where:* Timeline, By epic.
- **The sync brings the parents above your epics** (Jira). The Jira helper now also fetches the parents above what it syncs (Parent Link or parent), up to six levels, and writes them apart from your issues, so they never show up as work to sort. Copy the new sightline-jira-sync.py next to the plan. *Where:* The Jira helper.

## 1.84.0 · Sep 30, 2026

Rows by epic in the Days view.

### New

- **By epic in Days too** (Timeline). The Days view now has rows by epic as well: the same nesting, summary bars, and Expand all and Collapse all, with each story and task on its day. Still read-only, since the tree comes from Jira. *Where:* Timeline, Days, By epic (R).

## 1.83.0 · Sep 30, 2026

Timeline rows by epic.

### New

- **Rows by epic, nested** (Timeline). By epic puts one row per Jira epic, nested the way Jira's parent links nest, each with a bar spanning everything under it. Top epics open one level down; expand or collapse any row, or all of them. Work not under an epic sits on No epic, and a parent the sync didn't bring is named. It comes from Jira, so nothing drags there. *Where:* Timeline, Weeks, By epic (R).

## 1.82.2 · Sep 30, 2026

Jira stories by person, and keys that fit.

### Fixed

- **By person shows Jira stories** (Timeline). Each Jira story now sits on its assignee's row, in Weeks and Days, and counts toward what they have active. Unassigned stories go on Unassigned. An initiative carried by its stories no longer also sits on Unassigned. A plan run from Jira used to show almost nothing by person. *Where:* Timeline, By person.
- **Jira keys no longer run into names** (Timeline). When a task or story is too short for its name, its Jira key moves into the label to its right instead of being cut off inside the bar. *Where:* Timeline, Days view.

## 1.82.1 · Sep 29, 2026

Senior review 16: safer bulk sorting.

### Fixed

- **Bulk sort never counts stories nobody picked** (Jira). Sorting stories only groups them into their epic's initiative when the Jira files list all of that epic's stories, and only the ones on that list. Otherwise each story goes on by itself, so an initiative never counts stories you didn't pick. A parent that isn't an epic is no longer treated as one. *Where:* Plan setup, Sort Jira work.
- **Bulk sort respects what just changed** (Jira). Sorting a story from a parked epic brings the epic back with only that story. Every sort is decided again on the latest file, so a teammate's placement, epic link, parking or Not ours from a moment ago wins. Accept suggested is one save, so one Undo takes it all back, and number keys no longer also switch pages. *Where:* Plan setup, Sort Jira work.

## 1.82.0 · Sep 29, 2026

Plan setup, and fewer tabs for readers.

### Improved

- **Manage is now Plan setup, in four groups** (Plan). Manage is now Plan setup, and its 15 sections are grouped: Lists (Milestones, Gates, Decisions, Risks, Tags), Team (Team, Calendar, Meetings, Timeboxes & ceremonies), Jira (Sort Jira work, Proposals, Jira connection) and Reports (Status update, Snapshots, Activity). Jira work is now Sort Jira work, and Jira is Jira connection. Links to the old places still open. *Where:* Plan setup (was Manage).
- **Fewer tabs while you're reading** (Plan). Someone only reading a shared plan sees Today, Timeline, Sprint and Roadmap, with People and Plan setup under More. Start editing and all six are back. The page you're on always keeps its tab. *Where:* The tabs.

Today at a glance.

### New

- **A summary at the top of Today** (Today). Today now opens with a summary: what needs attention (to escalate, blocked, stale, late, should have started, decisions due; each jumps to its list), what's coming up (the next milestone and Jira release, and this quarter's deliverables with how many are at risk), and buttons to the Roadmap, Sprint and Timeline. The work queue follows below. *Where:* Today.

## 1.80.0 · Sep 29, 2026

A gentler first look.

### Improved

- **Clear next steps on an empty plan** (Timeline). Reconnecting a shared file is one clear button in the middle of the page. An empty shared plan you're reading says so and offers Start editing to set it up. An empty plan you're editing gets a short checklist (name it, name workstreams, add the first initiative, optionally bring in Jira and share it) that ticks itself off and goes away once there's work. *Where:* Timeline, on an empty or reconnecting plan.

Someone only reading a shared plan sees setup offers (like switching to Jira's sprints) as one quiet line, "1 setup note for whoever runs this plan · Show". Blockers, like reconnecting the file or recovering unsaved edits, still show in full, and editors see everything. *Where:* The notices under the header.

Start with your page.

### New

- **Start with** (Plan). Choose the page Sightline opens on: Today, My work (Today, just yours), Timeline, Sprint, Team capacity or Roadmap, or where you left off. It's yours, in this browser; links and reloads still open where they point. *Where:* File, then Start with.

## 1.78.0 · Sep 29, 2026

What a story serves.

### New

- **Serves on story cards** (Sprint). A Sprint card now says which deliverable its story is for ("Serves Faster checkout"), when the deliverable links the story itself or its feature or epic, so developers see the customer-facing thing behind the work. *Where:* Sprint tab cards.

## 1.77.0 · Sep 28, 2026

Sort Jira work in bulk.

### New

- **Sort Jira work into the plan, in bulk** (Jira). Jira work now offers Sort them in bulk: everything in a sprint or your searches that isn't on the plan, grouped by epic, sprint, assignee or label. Pick whole groups or Shift-click a range, then drop on a workstream, click it, press its number, or use Move to. Accept suggested sorts each group to where its people already have work. *Where:* Manage, then Jira work.

Stories you sort from the same epic become one initiative for that epic, with its other stories switched off, instead of one initiative per story: 70 stories under 10 epics are 10 initiatives. Dropping on an initiative adds them to it. Every drop is one save, with Undo. *Where:* Manage, then Jira work, Sort.

## 1.76.0 · Sep 28, 2026

Smoother everyday use.

### Improved

- **Before we commit: the sprint being planned, and a check before recording** (Sprint). Before we commit opens on the next sprint in the week before it starts, otherwise on the one running now. Recording a commitment while things are still flagged asks first and names them, so you can add an assumption. *Where:* Sprint tab.
- **What changed at a glance** (Today). Today says how many things changed right under its heading, with a link to the list; past the first 12 plan changes, See all opens Activity. The time Jira is compared from is in the panel's header. *Where:* Today.

The Deliverables row keeps a Roadmap link when only broader ones exist, and reads out ship days. The amendment editor names items instead of ids. Amendments open faster: what a date change moves is only worked out while their panel is open. *Where:* Manage, Timeline, Roadmap.

### Fixed

- **The status line reads properly** (Saving). The status line ran the file's state into the buttons' labels ("revision 73Start editingSave as you go"). It now shows just the state: "Read-only · Team.json · saved 3:02 PM · revision 73". *Where:* The status line at the bottom.

## 1.75.1 · Sep 28, 2026

Senior review 15.

### Fixed

- **Safer handling of odd plan files** (Plan). A plan whose id is a reserved word gets a safe one, so it can't disturb the page's settings. If teammates' snapshots merge past the limit of 12, none are dropped (adding a new one still waits until there's room). *Where:* Opening and merging plans.
- **Amendment edits you can trust** (Roadmap). Saving the editor no longer breaks an amendment that changes owners (owner lists aren't edited as text). If this browser can't store your edits, it says so and keeps the editor open instead of saying they were saved. Only recent batches' edits are kept. *Where:* Roadmap, Assistant amendments.
- **check-amendments refuses NaN** (Sync). The offline checker now refuses NaN and Infinity in an amendments file, as the page does, instead of calling it ready. *Where:* The sync script.
- **Smaller fixes** (Plan). A plan title can't add headings to the Markdown copy of a status update. A deliverable whose release ships before its Jira work's sprints now starts at its ship day on the Timeline, so the ship mark sits on its bar. *Where:* Status update; Timeline.

## 1.75.0 · Sep 28, 2026

Amendments for initiatives and tasks.

### New

- **Your assistant can amend initiatives and tasks** (Roadmap). Amendments can now add initiatives and tasks, and change their name, status, owners, workstream and dates. The review shows how many linked items a date change would move before you apply it. Jira-linked items keep Jira's status and dates (propose those in Jira instead), and dates that come from tasks can't be set directly. *Where:* Roadmap, Assistant amendments; the sync's check-amendments checks them too.

## 1.74.0 · Sep 28, 2026

Check amendments offline.

### New

- **check-amendments in the sync script** (Sync). The sync script can now check an amendments file against the plan without opening Sightline: python sightline-jira-sync.py check-amendments plan.json amendments.json. It uses the same rules as the page and lists each change as ready, changed since, invalid or already in the plan, with the reason; --json prints it for your assistant. The page still checks again when you apply. *Where:* The sync script; the guide in Export for your assistant says to use it.

Edit an amendment before applying it.

Deliverables in the Days view.

Before we commit.

Risks and decisions that move.

## 1.70.0 · Sep 28, 2026

Status update.

Snapshots.

- **Snapshots to compare against** (Plan). Save a named snapshot of the plan ("Q4 commit") and compare today with it: what's later or earlier and by how many working days, what was added, removed or dropped, what finished, and which deliverables were retimed. ## 1.68.0 · Sep 28, 2026

What changed.

### New

- **What changed since your last visit** (Today). Today now opens with what changed: teammates' plan changes (yours are summed up) and Jira's (done, started, changed sprint, new, release dates moved). Choose your last visit, yesterday or this week. Jira is compared with a daily summary of earlier syncs that this browser keeps; nothing goes into the plan file. *Where:* Today, top of the right column. Click a line to open it.

## 1.67.0 · Sep 28, 2026

Deliverables on the Timeline.

### New

- **A Deliverables row** (Timeline). Planned and done deliverables with a quarter, a date or a Jira release now show in a row under Releases. Each spans its linked Jira work's sprints and shows its progress; a release or date marks its ship day, and one with no sprint dates yet is a faint band across its quarter. Broader ones (a half, a year, Later) stay on the Roadmap and are counted in the row's header. *Where:* Timeline, weeks view. Click one to open it.

## 1.66.1 · Sep 28, 2026

Jira's facts stay Jira's.

### Fixed

- **Saving no longer copies Jira's status and sprint dates into the plan** (Jira). A save used to write Jira's status and sprint dates into the plan file as if someone had edited them. They now stay on screen only: saves, drafts, backups, downloads and merges keep the plan's own values. Jira's facts are applied again on every draw, so when Jira stops covering an item, the plan's own values come back. *Where:* Saving, Unsaved changes, Download JSON.

## 1.66.0 · Sep 28, 2026

Quick updates draw once.

### Improved

- **One redraw per quick update** (Saving). A quick update used to redraw the page twice: once while it was applied and again once it was saved. It now redraws once, when the save is confirmed, including after a retry because a teammate saved at the same moment. *Where:* Quick updates: status, notes, updates.

### Fixed

- **A refused quick update no longer stays on screen** (Saving). When a quick update couldn't be saved (for example, it would push the plan over 2 MB), the page kept showing the change even though the file didn't have it. It now shows the file's version, with the reason in the status line. *Where:* Quick updates.

## 1.65.0 · Sep 28, 2026

Undo that costs almost nothing.

### Improved

- **Undo kept as change records** (Saving). Undo used to keep a full copy of the plan for every step; older steps are now kept as the few hundred bytes that undo them, so a long editing session uses a fraction of the memory. Each step is checked when it's stored; the rare one that can't be described that way keeps its copy, so undo and redo are always exact. *Where:* Undo and Redo.
- **Bigger changes stay undoable from Activity** (Plan). Activity's Undo this now works for changes up to 96 KB (it was 16 KB), which covers a large Apply of assistant amendments. Anything bigger is listed as too big to undo from there, instead of the undo quietly disappearing. *Where:* Manage, Activity.

- **Hostile input is refused** (Saving). Amendment files can't use names that would change how the page works (like __proto__), odd values are refused rather than coerced, and link limits are enforced. Invalid wins over changed since. An add for an existing item must match everything it sets. Receipts follow what a change says, so an undone or rewritten change shows as Ready again. *Where:* Assistant amendments.

Plan format checks and a better Standup.

Safer saves and hides.

- **Drag milestones, gates and notes** (Timeline). Drag them along their row to another day. A click still opens them. A milestone that follows initiatives says so instead of moving. *Where:* Timeline, Days and Weeks.

## 1.17.0 · Sep 27, 2026

See what comes from Jira, and what was added here.

### New

- **From Jira and Added here look different** (Timeline). What comes from Jira is outlined in its workstream's color, with its Jira key. What was added here stays filled. This holds in Weeks, Days and the people rows, for initiatives, tasks and stories. The key explains both. *Where:* Timeline.
- **Show only what comes from Jira** (Timeline). Everyone / Jira only, next to the other view controls, shows the official Jira work on its own. A line under the controls says how many items added here are hidden, with Show everyone. Each plan remembers its own choice in your browser, and a saved view can keep it. *Where:* Timeline.

### Improved

- **Progress says what it counts** (Timeline). Bars show 5/9 stories for Jira work and 2/5 tasks (or items) for work added here, and the fill matches the count. The weighted percentage is in the hover and the card, marked as by task-days. *Where:* Timeline.
- **Jira's sprints and the plan's own timeboxes** (Sprints). When the plan follows Jira's sprints, a timebox the plan added (after Jira's last sprint, say) shows in italics. Hovering a Jira sprint shows Jira's exact dates. *Where:* Timeline sprint headers.
- **Parked initiatives are counted** (Timeline). A line says how many are parked, with a link to Plan, then Epics. *Where:* Timeline.

## 1.16.1 · Sep 27, 2026

Undo quick updates, and groups that stay open.

### Fixed

- **Undo works on Park, Put on the board, and switching stories** (Jira). Undo (and Ctrl+Z) reverses the last quick update in the shared file, key by key, so a teammate's newer changes stay. Redo puts it back, and a toast after each decision offers Undo. The Undo button names what it will undo. *Where:* Plan, then Epics; the initiative and story cards.
- **Epics groups stay the way you left them** (Jira). Each group remembers being opened or closed. *Where:* Plan, then Epics.

The weeks before Jira's first sprint say so, with a note on how to start the plan there instead. *Where:* Settings, then Jira, then Sprints from Jira.

Finished epics stay out of your way.

### New

- **Sightline knows when an epic is finished** (Jira). The sync counts the stories under every epic your searches find. An epic whose stories are all done or abandoned goes into a closed Finished in Jira group: it isn't in Unsorted, isn't counted as to sort, and isn't touched by Park all. A new epic with no stories yet stays in Unsorted. Each row says how many stories are open. *Where:* Plan, then Epics.
- **Park finished epics in one click** (Jira). When epics on the board are finished in Jira, Epics says how many and offers Park N finished. It keeps their initiatives and notes, and takes them off the timeline. *Where:* Plan, then Epics.

- **Counts for every epic a search finds** (Jira sync). Epics on the board are counted first (with their stories listed), then the other epics your searches found (counted only), all within the same 5,000-story limit. Copy the updated sightline-jira-sync.py and run install again. *Where:* sightline-jira-sync.py.

Sorting that respects your picks, and a lighter page.

## 1.15.0 · Sep 26, 2026

See whether Jira is keeping up.

When a watch is more than twice its interval late, the page says so and what to check: that the computer running it is on and signed in. It updates every minute while the page is open. *Where:* Plan, then Epics; and Settings.

Stories: counts that agree, and switches that stick.

When you open the page, the status line says Jira is paused until you reconnect. Plan opens on Epics for plans that use Jira. Your browser may offer to allow the folder on every visit, so you won't be asked again. *Where:* Plan, then Epics.

## 1.14.0 · Sep 26, 2026

An epic's stories, inside its initiative.

Stories have a dashed outline and their Jira key. Click one for its card. They're read-only, so change them in Jira. They aren't copied into the plan, and a story that's already a task in the plan shows as the task. *Where:* Timeline, Days view.

Off for now hides a story from the timeline and from progress, without changing Jira. Anyone can do it without Start editing, and two people's changes both count. Everyone should use this version, because older copies drop the list when they save. *Where:* The initiative's card, or the story's card.

- **Find and filters include stories** (Find). Find lists each story by its key, name and assignee. Status and people filters show the stories that match. *Where:* Find, and Filters.
- **The sync lists each epic's stories** (Jira sync). For epics on the board, the status file lists up to 3,000 stories with their sprint and status. Parked epics are counted but not listed. Copy the updated sightline-jira-sync.py and run install again. *Where:* sightline-jira-sync.py.

## 1.13.1 · Sep 26, 2026

Epic decisions that stick, and a sync that keeps going.

### Fixed

- **Park means parked** (Jira). Each epic belongs to one initiative, however it was linked. Park and Park all switch it off everywhere, and On… won't make a second initiative for an epic that's already on the board. *Where:* Plan, then Epics.
- **Messages say what really happened** (Jira). If it didn't save, your picks stay. In an editing session it says the change waits for Save. Back on explains when the epic's initiative was removed. *Where:* Plan, then Epics.
- **Scheduling leaves Jira stories in their sprint** (Timeline). Jira's sprint dates stay fixed when the plan schedules itself. A clash shows as a warning instead. *Where:* Timeline.
- **Statuses with a | in their name** (Jira). It's counted under its real name. Needs the updated sync script. *Where:* Epic progress and the status map.
- **watch keeps going** (Jira sync). A failure is reported for that plan only and retried after a minute, then less often. Only one watch runs on a computer, and one that loses the lock stops. *Where:* sightline-jira-sync.py watch.
- **sync --save changes only what you give it** (Jira sync). Each option replaces just that setting, and settings are saved only after a sync works. When several searches fill the file, the later ones say they were skipped. *Where:* sightline-jira-sync.py sync.

Jira keeps itself in sync, and every project carries its own jira folder.

Sightline survives being copied, and says so when it can't start.

The planner gets a name.

### New

- **Meet Sightline** (What's new). The planner is now called Sightline: your team's work, in plain sight. *Where:* The top left of the page and the browser tab.
- **One plan file your whole team shares** (Saving). Link a plan file your team shares. One person edits at a time, anyone can make quick updates, and nothing is overwritten without a backup. *Where:* File, then Link a file.
- **Your plan by lane or by person** (Timeline). See work by lane or by person, zoom from weeks to days, and plan around holidays and time off. *Where:* The Timeline and People tabs.
- **Sprints, meetings, and team rhythms** (Sprints & process). Set up sprints, repeating meetings, and process blocks like code freezes and releases that repeat every sprint from a rule. *Where:* Plan, then Sprints.
- **Jira status next to your plan** (Jira). Show each item's Jira status beside it. A small script fetches it, so the page never sees your token. *Where:* File, then Jira status.
